input: root is None or the root of a finite, acyclic binary tree with no shared child nodes. TreeNode is caller-supplied, with ordinary data fields val, left and right; val is an integer and each child is a TreeNode or None. Fields have no getters, proxies or concurrent mutations. The paired domain has at most 4294967295 nodes, so an append-only JavaScript array can represent the queue. Preconditions are not checked at runtime.
return: Maximum root-to-leaf path length in nodes; zero for an empty tree.
mutation_aliasing: No writes to nodes, values or child links. Input object identities and every alias held by the caller are preserved. The local queue borrows node references; no output node or container is allocated. The Solution instance retains no state.
numeric: Node values are exact integers in [-9007199254740991, 9007199254740991], excluding booleans and negative zero, and are never inspected. The result is a nonnegative Python int integer no larger than the node count. Depth, queue length and head arithmetic are exact within the paired domain. No bitwise coercion or floating-point value arithmetic is used.
complexity: O(n) worst-case time and O(n) auxiliary space for a nonempty n-node tree; O(1) for an empty tree. The append-only queue retains all enqueued references even after head advances, so space is not reported as O(width). Indexing and appends are constant/amortized constant time. There is no recursion or removal from the queue front.
source_accounting: The complete method and Solution wrapper are included. TreeNode is an explicit caller-owned input shape, not an uncharged helper implementation; this method constructs no nodes. No external library or hidden source expansion.
